items.title: View a Workspace
items.desc:
This tools allows you to access and/or search for a workspace.

A workspace can be accessed by entering the Workspace ID (WSID), along with the reason for accessing the workspace and selecting continue. If the user has permission, the user will be redirected to the client's workspace as a super administrator.

A workspace can all be accessed by searching based off a number of options and selecting the Access button. When selecting access, the user will be redirected to a page requesting the reason for accessing the workspace before selecting continue. If the user has permission, the user will be then redirected to the client's workspace as a super administrator.

Outside of accessing a workspace, this page can also provide useful information and allow users to View Details for a workspace entered in the search bar. These details include active modules, check count per check date, as well as a list of admins.

items.title: Custom Wage Type Request
items.desc:
This tool is designed for our support teams who need to request a new custom wage type for a specified client. 

It provides a structured, searchable interface for browsing and selecting from over 7,000 tax codes across Federal, State, and Local jurisdictions, then exporting those selections into a formatted Excel file. 

Start by entering one or more Workspace IDs, then choose the Custom Wage Type you are configuring:
  • Earning Select all taxes that should be EXEMPT from this wage type
  • Benefit/Deduction Select all taxes the benefit/deduction should be considered PRE-TAX for
  • Imputed Income Select all taxes the benefit should be SUBJECT TO

Enter a name or description for the wage type, then choose which main tax categories to work with, either Federal, State, Local, or any combination.

Tax codes are organized by Type, SubType, and State and are displayed in collapsible sections so you can focus on what's relevant. Within each section, you can select individual codes or use "Select all" at any level. Each grid supports filtering and sorting by any column.

When your selections are complete, export to Excel. The output includes a Summary sheet with your workspace details and all selected TaxIDs formatted for Postman, plus a detail sheet listing the full information for every selected tax code.

**Note** This is a temporary tool that will simplify these requests until a more permanent solution is released. Product has already discussed how to handle these going forward.

items.title: Payroll Migration Tool
items.desc:
This tool enables users to initiate a Payroll Data Migration (PDM) task.
A PDM task is specifically designed for clients transitioning from Dynamics GP and requires the payroll module to be active within the workspace. The PDM process occurs after a standard upsync task has been completed and executes the necessary GoFetch operations to transfer payroll data into the payroll database.
For Dynamics GP clients, please note that if a sync is executed on a workspace with the payroll module enabled, a PDM task will automatically be triggered following the completion of the upsyncÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂregardless of whether this tool is used. This tool is intended to streamline the process by allowing users to initiate the task without requiring direct access to the workspace.
It is also important to understand that a PDM task can only insert new records into the payroll database and cannot update existing ones. As a result, if a PDM task partially fails due to data or configuration issues, subsequent attempts may continue to fail even after those issues are resolved, as previously inserted records may be treated as duplicates.
To avoid this, it is recommended to run a standard sync with the payroll module disabled and resolve any errors prior to activating payroll. Addressing sync issues in a production workspace will also prevent those same issues from occurring in a beta workspace, eliminating the need to run a sync in beta before enabling the payroll module.

items.title: Sync Start Date
items.desc:
This configuration allows users to define a start date from which the sync process will retrieve data.

This setting is particularly useful in scenarios where historical data contains inconsistencies or errors that the client does not wish to correct. By specifying a start date, the sync can be limited to only include data from that point forward, avoiding issues tied to legacy data.

Example Use Case:
A client uses a single child support garnishment code for multiple child support records per employee. This is not supported, as each record requires a unique identifier. To resolve this, the client may update future payroll configurations by assigning distinct codes (e.g., Child Support 1 (CS1), Child Support 2 (CS2), etc.). By setting the sync start date to align with this change, only compliant data will be processed, preventing partial failures caused by duplicate records.

Please note that once a start date is configured, the sync process will only retrieve data from that date forward. Even if checksum tables are truncated to force a full sync, data prior to the specified start date will not be included.
items.config:
To request this setting, please send up a case with the below information:
 
WSID: The workspace ID(s) this setting needs to be configured for
Sync Start Date: The stating date the sync will look back from.
Reason: Detailed explanation as to why we are enabling this setting to ensure it fits the customer's needs.
